reported_snapshot.total_debt_note: Current portion $4.391B + long-term $31.090B at 2026-09-30 (10-Q). Excludes $70.97B of finance lease liabilities on the balance sheet. Does NOT yet include the $25B of notes priced 2026-10-29 (after quarter end); pro forma ~$60.5B (our arithmetic).
reported_snapshot.fcf_note: OCF $58.0B minus cash PP&E additions $39.4B = $18.6B (our arithmetic; matches FinSee/FourWeekMBA rebuild). Prior-year quarter ~$25.7B.
reported_snapshot.capex_guidance: CFO Hood: Q2 FY27 capex 'over $50 billion'; calendar-2026 spend ~ $170B (cut from ~$175B, citing third-party capacity delays). Expects to stay FCF-positive in FY27.
reported_snapshot.rpo_note: ~30% recognized in next 12 months; weighted avg duration ~2.3 years. Commercial RPO slipped $1B q/q from $678B.

off_balance_items.description: Leases, primarily datacenters, signed but not yet commenced; commence FY2027-FY2034 with 1-20 year terms; some subject to contractual conditions. Up from $329.1B at 2026-06-30. This alone is ~10x Microsoft's reported debt.
Purchase commitments from FY2026 10-K contractual obligations table (largely datacenter/cloud capacity and hardware; likely includes third-party GPU-as-a-service/neocloud contracts).
off_balance_items.source_title: Financial analysis of Microsoft FY2026 (sec-api.io, summarizing 10-K)
Financial analysis of Microsoft FY2026 (sec-api.io, summarizing 10-K)

off_balance_items.description: Nscale GPU capacity contract for Microsoft, up to ~$43.8B through Dec 2033 (per Nscale S-1). Bloomberg (Nov 2026) reports Microsoft walked away from a ~$3B Loughton UK site and declined an option to double Texas capacity. Likely overlaps with purchase commitments above.
Nebius GPU capacity contract, up to ~$17.4B over 5 years through 2031 (Nebius 20-F; originally reported as up to $19.4B). Likely overlaps with purchase commitments above.
off_balance_items.source_title: How Microsoft Rents AI Capacity: 3 Neocloud Deals, $70.9B

off_balance_items.description: IREN GPU cloud contract ~$9.7B through 2031 at Horizon (Texas); construction delays, timeline being renegotiated (Bloomberg, Nov 2026). Likely overlaps with purchase commitments above.

CoreWeave and Lambda capacity contracts: not individually disclosed. As of Oct 2025 Microsoft had signed >$33B with neoclouds in total (incl. Nebius ~$19.4B; remainder CoreWeave, Nscale, Lambda). Microsoft was 62% (FY24) and 67% (FY25) of CoreWeave revenue.
off_balance_items.source_title: Tom's Hardware; sec-api.io CoreWeave Q3 2026 analysis

off_balance_items.description: OpenAI share of commercial RPO: Microsoft disclosed 45% of $625B (~$281B) tied to OpenAI at 2025-12-31, after OpenAI's incremental $250B Azure commitment. NOTE: this ~45% figure is stale.
off_balance_items.source_title: Microsoft investors sweat cloud giant's OpenAI exposure (The Register)

off_balance_items.description: Updated estimate: ~32% (~$218B) of $678B commercial RPO tied to OpenAI, derived from CFO comment that RPO grew 25% ex-OpenAI. Microsoft does not disclose the exact share; for 2026-09-30 ($677B) FinSee says 'nearly half', unverified.
off_balance_items.source_title: Benzinga via Webull: Microsoft's backlog hit $678B

off_balance_items.description: Revenue from OpenAI commercial arrangements (incl. revenue-share) was $10.0B in the Sept-2026 quarter (~11% of revenue); OpenAI owed Microsoft $7.2B in receivables (up from $6.0B). OpenAI is itself heavily vendor-financed.

OpenAI equity investment: ~24% as-converted stake (equity method); total funding commitments $13.0B, of which $12.0B funded -> $1.0B remaining commitment. Equity-method carrying value is small vs. exposure.

Invest -> customer buys from you: Microsoft funded ~$12-13B into OpenAI, which in turn committed an incremental $250B to Azure (late-2025 restructuring) and pays Microsoft revenue share through 2030. Partnership loosened 2026-04-27 (non-exclusive license through 2032; Microsoft no longer pays OpenAI revenue share).
off_balance_items.source_title: Microsoft and OpenAI's open relationship is now official (The Register)

off_balance_items.description: Restricted investments held under a supplier agreement (Microsoft-funded collateral/prepayment to a supplier; nature not detailed). Up from $11.3B.
Reported discussion of a ~$250B financial backstop involving Nvidia for a Microsoft-backed OpenAI datacenter project in Ohio; terms and who backstops whom unclear; not confirmed as agreed.
IRS Notices of Proposed Adjustment seek an additional $28.9B tax payment plus penalties and interest (tax years 2004-2013); Microsoft is contesting.

total_note: Sum of hard, quantified non-debt commitments: leases not yet commenced $364.6B (9/30/26) + purchase commitments $194.1B (6/30/26) + construction commitments $34.6B (6/30/26) + remaining OpenAI funding commitment $1.0B = ~$594.2B. Neocloud contracts (~$70.9B Nscale/Nebius/IREN) are excluded as they are very likely inside purchase commitments. OpenAI RPO share, the $250B Azure commitment, receivables, the IRS claim, and the unconfirmed backstop are exposures/contingencies, not added. Dates are mixed (10-Q does not refresh purchase commitments). For scale: ~3.2x FY2026 operating cash flow (~$183B = FCF $67.0B + capex $115.9B) and ~17x reported debt of $35.5B.

credit_signals.detail: AAA (S&P) / Aaa (Moody's); one of only two US public companies with top ratings from both.
Priced $25B, 10-tranche senior unsecured notes (2- to 40-year) on 2026-10-29 -- first US IG bond since 2017 ($17B). Peak orders ~$115B (4.6x). Note: priced late Oct 2026 (settled around early Nov).
2066 notes at +105bp over Treasuries; 30-year at +95bp; long AAA paper yielding above 6%. One tranche carried a 6.150% coupon (per FourWeekMBA).
CreditSights estimated deal lifts gross lease-adjusted leverage to ~0.7x. CFO: will 'access additional sources of funding when we believe it is attractive'.

Moody's: 'unprecedented' AI spending threatens credit quality of six hyperscalers incl. Microsoft; group lease commitments ~$1.2T, >$820B not yet commenced, treated as debt-equivalent. No imminent downgrade expected.

news_context.headline_summary: Fiscal Q1 FY27: revenue $92.3B, Azure +48%, commercial RPO $677B (+73%), capex $45.2B incl. finance leases; calendar-2026 capex trimmed to ~$170B; third-party GPU contracts delayed to H2.
news_context.why_it_matters: Demand is strong but spending is now far above free cash flow growth, and delays at neocloud suppliers show the build-out is supply-chain fragile.

news_context.headline_summary: 10-Q shows datacenter leases signed but not commenced jumped to $364.6B from $329.1B one quarter earlier.
news_context.why_it_matters: This is the largest hidden obligation -- ~10x reported debt -- and it is invisible to debt/EBITDA scoring until each lease starts.

news_context.headline_summary: Microsoft sold $25B of bonds in 10 tranches, its first US bond since 2017, with ~$115B of orders.
news_context.why_it_matters: Even an AAA cash machine is now borrowing to fund AI capex; demand was strong, so credit markets are still open for top names.

news_context.headline_summary: Microsoft earned $10.0B from OpenAI arrangements in the quarter (~11% of revenue); OpenAI owes it $7.2B.
news_context.why_it_matters: A large, growing slice of revenue and receivables depends on one customer that is itself loss-making and financed by its suppliers.

news_context.headline_summary: Bloomberg: Microsoft stepping back from ~$70.9B of neocloud deals (Nscale, Nebius, IREN) facing delays; walked from a ~$3B UK site; IREN -18%, Nebius -16%, CoreWeave -12%.
news_context.why_it_matters: Shows Microsoft can push risk back onto leveraged suppliers -- good for Microsoft, bad for the neoclouds whose debt relies on Microsoft contracts.

news_context.headline_summary: Big Tech (Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) raised $253.4B of new long-term debt in nine months, ~45% of capex vs ~17% a year earlier.
news_context.why_it_matters: Confirms the thesis that the build-out is increasingly debt-financed, even at the strongest balance sheets.

news_context.headline_summary: Moody's warns hyperscaler AI spending threatens credit quality; counts unstarted leases as debt-like.
news_context.why_it_matters: Rating agencies already adjust for the leases a balance-sheet-only app misses.

hidden_leverage_assessment.rationale: On its own books Microsoft looks nearly debt-free ($35.5B of debt vs $64.5B of cash), which is why a balance-sheet scorer rates it a fortress. But it has signed roughly $365B of datacenter leases that haven't started yet plus ~$230B of purchase and construction commitments -- about 3x a year of operating cash flow. A big chunk of its $677B backlog (45% at end-2025, maybe ~a third now) comes from OpenAI, a money-losing customer that Microsoft helped fund. Microsoft still generates strong positive free cash flow and has AAA ratings, so it can absorb a lot, but the cushion is shrinking as it now borrows to build.
hidden_leverage_assessment.biggest_hidden_risk: If OpenAI cannot raise the money to honor its ~$250B Azure commitment, Microsoft is left with hundreds of billions in non-cancelable leases and GPUs built for a customer that isn't paying.
hidden_leverage_assessment.what_would_change_my_mind: A disclosed, sharply lower OpenAI share of RPO (diversified backlog) together with capex coming back under operating cash flow would push this to Moderate; OpenAI funding trouble or lease commitments rising past ~$450B would push it to High.
